stories.headline: PM-HM jodi lying, special sitting not for women's quota but delimitation: Congress
stories.deck: The Opposition party said the government is convening a session, slated to begin on November 30, on the delimitation bill, which it will firmly oppose
stories.bodyText:
The Congress on Friday (November 27, 2026) said the upcoming special session of Parliament has little to do with women's reservation and is a desperate move by a "nervous and rattled" Prime Minister.
The Opposition party said the government is convening a session, slated to begin on November 30, on the delimitation bill, which it will firmly oppose.
"Yet again, the mischievous PM-HM jodi is lying," Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said on X.
The former Union Minister pointed out that the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam to give one-third reservation to women was passed unanimously by Parliament in September 2023, and the Congress president had demanded its immediate implementation, but in vain.
The law did not get notified till 10:40 pm on April 16, 2026, Mr. Ramesh said.
"The Special Session is thus NOT for women's reservation. That is already a law which the PM-HM jodi have put into cold storage for over three years," he said.
Mr. Ramesh alleged that the special session is for delimitation, to carve out constituencies to benefit the BJP.
"And who will be in charge of deciding the geography of constituencies? It will be a thoroughly compromised and brutally exposed CEC, Gyanesh Kumar, who has made a complete mockery of the preparation of electoral rolls and destroyed the integrity of the electoral process," Mr. Ramesh said.
"The executors of Vote Chori on such a gigantic scale are to be given the powers to carry out delimitation and manipulate the nature of constituencies. This is as atrocious as you can get.
"This is a desperate move by a nervous and rattled PM who is under siege. It will be countered with firm resolve," the Congress leader added.
Mr. Ramesh's remarks came a day after the government proposed a special sitting of Parliament to transact "essential" business, amid indications that the delimitation-linked women's reservation bill may be reintroduced.
Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju on Thursday (November 26, 2026) said the government has requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the two Houses on November 30 and on December 2, in that order.
"Subject to exigencies of the business, the sitting of both Houses may conclude on December 3, 2026," he wrote on X.
The sitting will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, since Parliament was adjourned sine die on August 13 and never prorogued, the formal ending of a session.
The Congress has alleged that, with the special sitting, the PM Modi government hopes to use its "super-tainted" two-thirds majority to pass the Constitutional amendment bill.
Mr Ramesh said on Thursday (November 26) that the PM Modi government made the delimitation bills public on April 14, Ambedkar Jayanti, and that they were defeated on April 17, a "well-deserved" outcome.
"Now on Constitution Day, after 105 days of Operation Lotus, PM Modi government announces a special session, hoping that it will get its super-tainted two-thirds majority to pass a Constitution amendment bill," he said.
Can there be a greater insult to and assault on the Constitution? Mr. Ramesh wondered and asserted, "The fight is on."

stories.headline: 'Delimitation will prove to be BJP's biggest political mistake': Akhilesh Yadav
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
Samajwadi Party
 chief 
Akhilesh Yadav
 on Friday attacked the ruling 
BJP
 over the proposed delimitation-linked women's reservation bill, saying it would prove to be the party's “biggest political mistake”.
“Delimitation will prove to be the biggest political mistake made by the BJP,” Akhilesh said in a post on X.
His remarks came a day after the government announced a special sitting of Parliament from November 30 to December 3 to transact “essential” business, amid speculation that it may reintroduce the delimitation-linked women's reservation bill.
The proposed legislation seeks to increase the Lok Sabha's strength from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats through delimitation, paving the way for the implementation of 33% reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures ahead of the 2029 general elections.
‘Mischievous PM-HM jodi is lying’
Congress also alleged that the special session had little to do with women's reservation and accused the government of using it to push the delimitation bill.
“Yet again, the mischievous PM-HM jodi is lying,” Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said on X.
Ramesh pointed out that the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, providing one-third reservation for women, was passed unanimously by Parliament in September 2023.
The Congress president had subsequently demanded its immediate implementation, but the law was not notified until 10.40 pm on April 16, 2026, he said.
“The Special Session is thus NOT for women's reservation. That is already a law which the PM-HM jodi have put into cold storage for over three years,” Ramesh said.
He alleged that the government was convening Parliament to push delimitation and redraw constituencies to benefit the BJP.
“And who will be in charge of deciding the geography of constituencies? It will be a thoroughly compromised and brutally exposed CEC, Gyanesh Kumar, who has made a complete mockery of preparation of electoral rolls and destroyed the integrity of the electoral process,” he said.
“The executors of Vote Chori on such a gigantic scale are to be given the powers to carry out delimitation and manipulate the nature of constituencies. This is as atrocious as you can get.
“This is a desperate move by a nervous and rattled PM who is under siege. It will be countered with firm resolve,” Ramesh added.
The Congress has also alleged that the government is hoping to secure a “super-tainted” two-thirds majority to pass the Constitution amendment bill.
‘Thackeray is no more, Pawar is unwell’: Shiv Sena (UBT)
Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut also opposed the proposed delimitation exercise, alleging that it was a BJP conspiracy to take away people's political power.
Sharing a post on X, Raut said, “Today, Shiv Sena chief Balasaheb Thackeray is no longer with us: Sharad Pawar is unwell and in no position to fight or make decisions, otherwise the anti-national Delimitation Bill would never have dared to be brought before Parliament in such a corrupt manner: Delimitation is a BJP conspiracy to strip the people of this country of their power.”
“Anyone who supports it is betraying the people of this country… They will be known as the biggest traitors of the 21st century! Therefore, every patriotic, democratic party should reject Delimitation in Parliament. History always remembers the names of traitors; Explanations for betrayal fade into thin air” he added.
Meanwhile, the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) is likely to support the delimitation bill, provided it ensures regional balance, party sources told ANI.
Decoding delimitation maths
The Lok Sabha Secretariat said the second part of the eighth session of the 18th Lok Sabha will begin on November 30. The special sitting is expected to conclude on December 3, subject to the exigencies of government business.
The sittings will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13 but not prorogued.
Earlier on Thursday, Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Houses to transact essential government business.
The Union Cabinet is also scheduled to meet on Friday and is likely to discuss the delimitation-linked women's reservation legislation, sources said.
The developments follow Prime Minister Narendra Modi's remarks on Thursday, accusing an opposition party of blocking the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, in April.
In a signed article published in newspapers, PM Modi, “The journey of our Constitution would be incomplete without recognising the remarkable women who helped shape it. But what happened earlier this year should fill our hearts with shame.”
“I assure the 'Nari Shakti' of India that no force can prevent us from ensuring that justice is done to them,” he added.
The bill was defeated in April after the government failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha. It needs 361 votes in the 543-member House, which currently has 540 members due to three vacancies.
The NDA has around 320 MPs and would require additional support from opposition parties to cross the threshold.
The government's position has strengthened since the bill's defeat in April, with 26 MPs moving out of the opposition camp.
Twenty rebel Trinamool Congress MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA, while six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.

However, the ruling alliance still needs additional votes. The DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (SP), with eight, could play a significant role in the evolving political arithmetic.
Opposition parties are also expected to raise their protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, potentially leading to another stormy session.

stories.headline: Why Has Your Car Insurance Renewal Premium Changed Despite Making No Claims?
stories.bodyText:
Your renewal premium can rise even if you have not made a claim because your claim history is only one part of the calculation. Insurers also consider the car's value, repair risks, type of cover, policy discounts and applicable third-party rates.
Experience a more refined e-paper today
A claim-free year may reduce one portion of the premium without reducing the total amount. The following reasons explain where the difference may come from and what to check before renewing.
Insurers periodically review the cost of settling claims across different types of vehicles. Higher repair bills, replacement part costs or claims experience involving similar cars can affect their own-damage rates. Your personal record may be unchanged, but the rate used to calculate your renewal might be different.
The insured declared value (IDV) represents your car's value for certain major loss claims. It is reviewed at renewal and usually reduces as a vehicle ages. Changes in IDV can alter the own-damage premium.
An increase in the overall renewal amount is still possible when the IDV falls, because other pricing factors may move in the opposite direction. Check the IDV on both policy schedules and ensure the renewal figure is appropriate for your vehicle.
The premium for mandatory third-party liability cover is separate from the own-damage portion. It follows the rates applicable to the vehicle's category and engine capacity. If a prescribed rate changes, or your car has been placed in the wrong category, the renewal amount can differ even without a claim.
Check this component separately. A claim-free record does not create a discount on the mandatory third-party premium. When examining the quote, keep this statutory portion separate from optional benefits, since changes in one do not explain changes in the other.
The no claim bonus in car insurance applies to the eligible own-damage premium, not the entire bill. It rises with consecutive claim-free periods only up to the permitted maximum. Once you reach that level, another claim-free year does not increase the discount further.
A bonus may also be missing because the insurer has not verified your previous policy details or because renewal was delayed beyond the permitted period.
Renewal quotes may include benefits that were absent from your earlier policy. Zero depreciation, roadside assistance, engine protection or other optional covers can affect the total amount. Conversely, a removed benefit may reduce the premium but leave you with less protection.
Read the benefits listed in each schedule. Do not assume two policies provide the same cover simply because both are described as comprehensive.
A voluntary deductible is the amount you agree to pay towards an eligible claim, in addition to any compulsory deductible. Choosing a higher voluntary deductible can reduce the own-damage premium. If you selected one previously but not this year, the renewal amount may increase.
Check the deductible amount rather than focusing only on the quoted premium. Your contribution at claim time matters too. A lower deductible may leave the insurer paying more towards repairs and can increase the premium.
Insurers use details such as registration location, vehicle age, model and modifications when assessing risk. An address update, a declared modification or an incorrect entry can change the quotation. Even a small mismatch deserves correction before payment.
Confirm that the insurer has used the details shown in your registration certificate and previous policy. If you recently moved or altered the vehicle, make sure those changes have been recorded accurately.
Your car insurance renewal premium may change even when you have not made any claims. Factors such as revised insurance rates, vehicle value, additional coverage and deductibles can affect the final amount.
Before renewing, review your previous and current policy details to identify the reason for the difference. If the change is unclear, contact your insurer for a detailed explanation to make an informed renewal decision.

briefs.headline: Madras High Court permits byelections only in Ambasamudram and Perundurai constituencies in Tamil Nadu
briefs.deck: Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan say bypolls to Tiruchi East, Karur, and Viralimalai will have to wait till orders could be passed in related election petitions
briefs.bodyText:
The Madras High Court on Friday (November 27, 2026) permitted the conduct of byelections to the Ambasamudram and Perundurai Assembly constituencies alone and ordered that the bypolls to the Tiruchi East, Viralimalai, and Karur constituencies would have to wait until appropriate orders were passed on the election petitions pending with respect to them.
The First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan partly allowed a public interest litigation (PIL) petition filed by Tirunelveli-based advocate K. Venkatachalapathy alias Kutty, through his counsel V.R. Shanmuganathan, for deferring the bypolls to the five constituencies until the disposal of the election petitions.
The necessity to conduct a bypoll in Tiruchi East had arisen because Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay had won from two constituencies but decided to resign from this seat and retain Perambur. Insofar as Viralimalai, Karur, Ambasamudram, and Perundurai were concerned, C. Vijayabaskar, M.R. Vijayabhaskar, Esakki Subaya, and S. Jayakumar had won, respectively, as AIADMK candidates but submitted their resignations to the Speaker before joining the ruling TVK.
The PIL petitioner’s argument was that all five election petitioners before the court had not only challenged the victory of the MLAs concerned but also filed applications for declaring either the petitioners or other candidates as the returned candidates from those constituencies. Therefore, the conduct of byelections before the disposal of the election petitions might lead to an anomalous situation, the petitioner feared.
He said, each of those constituencies might end up having two representatives if someone else gets declared as the elected candidate by the High Court after the conduct of the bypolls. Finding prima facie force in the argument, the Chief Justice’s Bench had passed an interim order on July 10, 2026, restraining the Election Commission of India (ECI) from holding bypolls in the five constituencies.
Thereafter, Chief Electoral Officer Archana Patnaik filed a counter affidavit in August 2026 stating that the ECI does not intend to hold bypolls in the five constituencies until the disposal of the election petitions concerned. However, after Justice D. Bharatha Chakravarthy rejected an election petition with respect to Perundurai on September 8, 2026, the ECI said, bypoll could be held for that constituency alone if the court vacates the interim stay.
Subsequently, Justice P.B. Balaji cleared the decks for the conduct bypoll in Ambasamudram constituency on October 1, 2026. Though the judge refused to reject the election petition with respect to that constituency, he struck off the plea to declare the runner-up as the winner and ordered that the bypolls need not be deferred until the conclusion of the trial.
During the course of final arguments on the PIL plea, senior counsel Dama Seshadri Naidu told the court that the ECI does not consider the case as an adversarial litigation and that it would abide by any order passed by the court. In the meantime, the Chief Minister urged the court to vacate the interim stay on bypolls since the people could not remain unrepresented in the Legislative Assembly for long.

briefs.headline: Governor Arlekar writes to CM Vijay expressing concerns over Vice-Chancellor vacancies in State universities
briefs.deck: Arlekar flags the consequential delay in conducting convocations, which affect the day-to-day administration of the universities
briefs.bodyText:
Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar on Thursday wrote to Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay expressing concerns about the prolonged vacancies in the posts of Vice-Chancellors in several State universities and the consequential delay in conducting convocations, which affect the day-to-day administration of the universities, and sought his personal intervention in resolving the issues.
In his letter, a copy of which was circulated to the media, Mr. Arlekar pointed out administrative decisions relating to [many] universities were currently being taken through a Convenor Committee constituted by the State government. However, this arrangement had not been found effective in addressing the day-to-day administrative and academic requirements of individual universities, which necessitated decisions at the institutional level.
Therefore, it was important to put in place suitable arrangements for the appointment of full-time Vice-Chancellors, in accordance with the respective University Acts and UGC Regulations, to ensure effective administration and continuity of academic activities. “Simultaneously, a university-wise schedule could be drawn up to conduct all pending convocations at the earliest, wherever legally permissible, so that students were not further disadvantaged,” the Governor said.
The principal issue related to the composition of Search-cum-Selection Committees, particularly the inclusion of a nominee of the Chairman, University Grants Commission (UGC), under Regulation 7.3(ii) of the UGC Regulations, 2018. The differing positions of the State government and the Chancellor had resulted in related judicial proceedings, the Governor pointed out.
In this context, the judgment of the Supreme Court in Dr. S. Mohan v. Secretary to the Chancellor, Puducherry Technological University, dated January 30, 2026, assumed significance, he said. The then Governor-Chancellor had, through a press release on February 2, 2026, requested the inclusion of the UGC nominee in the Search Committees and that ongoing selection proceedings be kept in abeyance pending the outcome of the related judicial proceedings, Mr. Arlekar said.
With a view to resolving the matter through mutual consultation and establishing a transparent and merit-based selection mechanism, the Governor proposed for constituting a Search-cum-Selection Committee comprising a nominee each of the Chancellor, the University Syndicate, the UGC Chairman, and of the State government, subject to applicable statutory provisions and judicial directions. The members should be distinguished academicians and experts with proven integrity and professional standing.
He said the Committee should initiate the process preferably six months before the anticipated vacancy, advertise the post within 15 days of its constitution, and complete scrutiny and interviews within two months of the advertisement. Most importantly, the Committee should, by unanimous decision, shortlist three eligible candidates and rank them in order of preference, he suggested.
“I am confident that, through mutual consultation and cooperation, an early and legally sustainable resolution can be achieved. I seek your personal intervention to facilitate the proposed mechanism and expedite the pending convocations, in the larger interest of universities and the thousands of students awaiting their degrees,” Mr. Arlekar added.

briefs.headline: SIT’s chargesheet gives clean chit to Nagendra in Valmiki Corporation scam
briefs.bodyText:
Former minister and ex-corporation chairman Basavaraj Daddal named as witnesses in final chargesheet filed before Lokayukta Special Court
In a major departure from the findings of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Directorate of Enforcement (ED), the Karnataka Special Investigation Team (SIT) has found no evidence linking former Minister B. Nagendra to the alleged misappropriation of ₹89.62 crore from the Valmiki Corporation, and has named him as a witness, and not an accused, in its final chargesheet.
The chargesheet, filed before the Lokayukta Special Court on November 25, under the Prevention of Corruption Act, also names former corporation chairman Basavaraj Daddal as a witness.
The SIT’s findings effectively give Nagendra a clean chit in the alleged fund diversion, in contrast to the separate investigations by the CBI and the ED, both of which have implicated him. The CBI has described him as prime accused in the scam, while the ED has also accused him of involvement in the financial irregularities.
Mr. Nagendra was Minister for Scheduled Tribes Welfare when the alleged scam came to light. He resigned from the Cabinet following the controversy and was subsequently arrested by the ED. After being re-inducted into the Cabinet, he resigned again in August this year.
Reacting to the SIT’s findings, Home Minister Priyank Kharge said the investigation was based on evidence and that no money trail linking Nagendra to the alleged misappropriation had been established.
The alleged scam came to light following the suicide of Chandrashekar P, the corporation’s accounts superintendent, at his residence in Shivamogga on May 26, 2024. His death brought to light the alleged diversion of ₹89.62 crore from the corporation.
The SIT was constituted to investigate both the alleged financial irregularities and Chandrashekar’s death. In its first chargesheet, filed in August 2024, the SIT did not name Nagendra as an accused in the alleged fund diversion. It charged several others, including Padmanabha, Parashuram Durgannanavar, a former accounts officer of the corporation, Sathyanarayana Etakari, Nekkunte Nagaraj, Nageshwar Rao, M Chandramohan and several others from Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
The accused also included Satyanarayana Varma and Saiteja from Hyderabad, G.K. Jagadish from Shivamogga, Teja Thammaiah from Bengaluru, and Pittala Srinivasa and Khaki Srinivasa Rao from Andhra Pradesh.
In a second chargesheet, the SIT invoked abetment of suicide and SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) charges against two others in connection with Chandrashekar’s death, but concluded that Chandrashekar had died by suicide.
Despite clean chit, Mr. Nagendra continue to be in the dock as the CBI and ED are continuing their separate investigations into the alleged scam.

briefs.headline: Chennai entrepreneur Vardhman Jain donates 121 kg gold ornaments worth ₹207.6 crore to Tirumala temple
briefs.deck: Vardhman Jain says he funded the 121 kg gold donation to Tirumala from the proceeds of selling his company to a New York-based private equity firm
briefs.bodyText:
In what is believed to be the largest offering to the presiding deity in recent times, Vardhman Jain, co-founder of Chennai-based Access Healthcare, donated gold ornaments weighing 121 kg, valued at approximately ₹207.6 crore, to Lord Venkateswara at Tirumala on Thursday (November 26, 2026).
Mr. Jain, accompanied by his wife Radhika Vardhman Jain and his brother Anurag Jain, the company’s other co-founder, handed over the offering to the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) authorities in the presence of Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu inside the hill temple.
Speaking to the media, Mr. Jain said he had decided to donate 121 kg of gold to the temple from the proceeds of the sale of his company to a New York-based private equity firm. The firm, New Mountain Capital, acquired a majority stake in Access Healthcare in January 2025, in a deal that Bloomberg reported valued the company at about $2 billion.
He said the choice of 121 kg was itself a divine coincidence, as he had not consciously arrived at the figure. Coincidentally, the gold ornaments that adorn the presiding deity every day also weigh 121 kg.
Mr. Jain thanked the Chief Minister’s Office for closely monitoring the progress of the offering and following up every week.
Of the total 121 kg of gold, 106 kg has been used to craft an array of ornaments for the presiding deity, including a diamond-studded golden crown, ‘Padma Peetham’, ‘Kati-Varada hastams’ and ‘Karnabharanams’. The remaining 15 kg of pure gold will be used to make a golden saree for Goddess Padmavati Ammavaru at Tiruchanoor.
Carried to the sanctum
After darshan, Mr. Naidu, the donor couple and their family viewed the ornaments, 46 pieces of 33 types, displayed at the Ranganayakula Mandapam. Members of the family then carried them on plates over their heads, went around the Dhwajastambham and placed them before the deity in the sanctum sanctorum.
Among the pieces are a pair of ‘Pada Kavachams’ (covers for the deity’s feet), anklets, covers for the conch and discus (‘Sankha’ and ‘Chakra Kavachams’), a serpent-motif waist belt (‘Nagabharana Vaddanam’), armlets (‘Bhujakeerthulu’), a tiger-claw pendant (‘Puligoru’), ear ornaments and necklaces set with saligrama stones, according to the TTD. The value of ₹207.6 crore includes making charges, it said.
The ornaments incorporate 2,916.5 precious stones, including 2,247.7 carats of blue sapphires, 91.6 carats of yellow sapphires, 84.2 carats of rubies and emeralds, besides 238.2 carats of diamonds.

briefs.headline: 'Arrest me': CJP's Dipke dares Mumbai Police, defies lookout circular at Nagpur rally
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder and national convener Abhijeet Dipke on Thursday addressed a protest rally in Nagpur, challenging 
Mumbai Police
 to arrest him. The rally came even as Mumbai Police issued a Look Out Circular (LOC) against him in connection with an FIR linked to the party’s October 2 protest in Mumbai.
"There is a lookout notice against me by the Mumbai Police. There is police bandobast here and they are looking for me. Where is Abhijeet Dipke? I am here in Samvidhan Chowk. What will you do? Arrest me,” Dipke said, according to news agency ANI.
“I have been in jail twice. Don't show me the fear of jail," he added, while addressing the CJP's 'Save Democracy, Save Constitution' rally at Samvidhan Chowk on Constitution Day.
Mumbai Police issued LOCs against Dipke and CJP co-convenors Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das on Thursday. The circulars are linked to an FIR registered at Shivaji Park police station on October 3 over the party's protest held the previous day.
The FIR names the organisers and between 400 and 500 unidentified attendees, invoking Sections 189 and 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), relating to unlawful assembly and disobedience to an order promulgated by a public servant.
At the Nagpur rally, Dipke accused the BJP-led Centre of undermining the Constitution and alleged that institutions across the country had been hijacked.
"The government is acting against the Constitution. Not a single institution is left that has not been hijacked," he said.
He also warned against what he described as the government's use of intimidation. "You have destroyed the country by intimidating people but this will not be tolerated. Show as much fear as you want for two more years. 2029 is approaching. This is India after Jantar Mantar," Dipke said.
CJP co-convenor Ranka said the party would expand its activities beyond protests in major cities. "We will go to every village, interact with people and give a voice to the youth," he said.

The LOCs come amid a separate legal challenge by Das, who was stopped from boarding a flight to the United Kingdom at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport on November 23. He was scheduled to attend a panel discussion at Oxford.

briefs.headline: Women will get 33% reservation, Congress cannot stop it: Amit Shah
briefs.deck: The Home Minister says the Bharatiya Janata Party, under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is committed to ensuring political representation for women
briefs.bodyText:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday (November 26, 2026) accused the Congress of obstructing the implementation of 33% reservation for women legislators in Parliament and State Assemblies, and said neither the party nor its leader Rahul Gandhi would be able to prevent its implementation.
“The women of this country will definitely get 33% reservation. You cannot stop us,” Mr. Shah said, attacking Mr. Gandhi, the Leader of the Opposition.
His statement on the Women’s Reservation Act, which the government has linked to the passage of the Delimitation Bill, came hours before Parliamentary Minister Kiren Rijiju announced the reconvening of the Parliament Session on November 30.
In April, the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, which sought to redistribute Lok Sabha seats on the basis of the 2011 Census to expedite the implementation of women’s reservation, was defeated by the Opposition.
The Home Minister said the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, was committed to ensuring political representation for women.
‘UCC in all BJP-ruled States’
Mr. Shah reiterated the BJP’s commitment to implementing the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in States governed by the party, saying the Constitution’s framers had included the principle in the Directive Principles of State Policy.
He said citizens should be governed by a common civil law irrespective of their religious identity and argued that laws should not be framed based on religion. Our Constitution framers included the UCC in our Directive Principles. Every single citizen in this country — irrespective of religion, whether Hindu, Sikh, Muslim, Christian, or Parsi must get the right to live under one uniform law,” Mr. Shah said.
He added that BJP governments would move to implement the UCC in their States .“Today I have come to state with clarity that in the coming days, wherever there are BJP-ruled governments, we are going to implement the UCC,” he said, while delivering an address at the ‘Samvidhan Gaurav Diwas’ programme organised by the Delhi State BJP on the ocassion of Constitution Day.
‘Respect the Constitution’
Indirectly taking potshots at Mr. Gandhi, Mr. Shah said that merely carrying a copy of the Constitution or displaying it in public did not amount to respecting it. He said constitutional values must be reflected in the conduct of individuals, political parties and those holding public office. “There are two ways to respect the Constitution. One is to carry it and respect the book; another is to abide by its principles as an individual and as a political party,” Mr. Shah said.
He accused Mr. Gandhi of criticising constitutional institutions, including the courts and the Election Commission, and of demanding discussions on the streets rather than in Parliament. He accused the Congress leader of attempting to discredit electoral processes, including the special intensive revision of electoral rolls.
Mr. Shah said elections can be won only by understanding the pulse of the people, whereas every third month Mr. Gandhi is on a foreign vacation. “Criticising India while speaking abroad is not how you show your respect towards the Constitution.”
“You will have to win people’s trust,” Mr. Shah said, adding that the Congress had imposed the Emergency and “locked the Constitution for 18 months.”
He said Constitution can be preserved only if people follow their duties. Reiterating the BJP’s commitment to make the country developed by 2047, Mr. Shah recalled a conversation with a Congress leader in Parliament. “A Congress leader who met me in Parliament said that Modi ji will not be there in 2047. I told him you are merely looking at an individual; we are concerned about Bharat Mata. This Sankalp [resolution] is about making the country great, not an individual,” Mr. Shah said.
Mr. Shah said the Constitution’s principles included inclusion, reach and dignity. “Just in 12 years of BJP government, Prime Minister Modi has given 80 crore poor people a bank account, electricity in their homes, toilets, drinking water, a ₹5 lakh health scheme, LPG cylinders and 5 kg of free ration,” he said.
He said digital services had improved the reach of government schemes and enabled benefits to be delivered directly to people.
On national security, Mr. Shah cited the abrogation of Article 370, the decline of Left-wing extremism and the surrender of armed groups in the Northeast as measures taken by the government to strengthen national unity. He said around 11,000 people in the Northeast had surrendered their weapons and joined the mainstream.

stories.headline: Bengaluru man pays Rs 2 lakh to book residential plot, cancels deal over missing legal documents; builder fails to refund despite written assurance, consumer commission orders Rs 2 lakh refund with 9% interest and Rs 25,000 compensation
stories.deck: A Bengaluru consumer commission directed a real estate company to refund Rs 2 lakh to a man. This decision came after the company failed to provide necessary property documents for a residential plot. The man, who had made an advance payment, requested the refund after cancellation. Despite acknowledging their liability, the company did not process the refund as promised.
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: A Bengaluru consumer commission has directed a real estate company and its two directors to refund Rs 2 lakh to a 41-year-old man who cancelled the booking of a residential plot after the builder allegedly failed to provide essential property documents. The commission also ordered them to pay Rs 25,000 towards compensation and litigation expenses.
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (Bengaluru Urban), in an order dated October 7, directed Virtue Infra Builders Pvt Ltd and its directors, R M Harikrishna and Aravinda Kumar, to refund the booking amount with 9% annual interest from July 19, 2024, until payment.
The commission also ordered the opposite parties to pay Rs 10,000 for deficiency in service, Rs 10,000 for pain and suffering, and Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs. They have been given 45 days to comply with the order.
According to the complaint filed by Muni Rao, he had approached the company to purchase a residential plot in its Virtue Star City project at Mathkur village in Bengaluru North. Based on the company's representations about the property's title, approvals and availability for immediate registration, he agreed to purchase plot No. 66, measuring 1,410 sq ft.
On July 19, 2024, Rao paid Rs 2 lakh as advance booking amount, comprising Rs 1.5 lakh through cheque and Rs 50,000 through an online transaction.
However, after receiving the payment, the company allegedly failed to provide the complete legal documents required to verify the title and legality of the transaction. These included mother deeds and title documents, land conversion order, approved layout plan, RERA approval and e-Khata documents.
Unable to verify the property's legal status, Rao decided to cancel the booking and sought a refund. Despite repeated requests, phone calls and emails, the company did not return the money, according to the complaint.
On August 21, 2024, the company acknowledged its liability to refund the booking amount through an email and assured Rao that the money would be credited by November 20, 2024. It also apologised for the delay and assured him that the refund would be processed. However, the payment was not made even after the promised deadline, forcing him to approach the consumer commission.
The commission noted that the builder and its directors failed to appear before it despite receiving notice and did not file their written version. The matter was consequently heard ex parte.
After examining the complainant's affidavit and supporting documents, the commission observed that the company had failed to furnish the necessary property documents despite receiving the advance amount. It also noted that the company had acknowledged its liability to refund the money but had failed to honour its assurance.
The commission held the company and its two directors jointly and severally liable, observing that the complainant was neither given possession of the plot nor refunded the deposited amount. It concluded that their conduct amounted to deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.

stories.headline: Don’t threaten govt, end stir, CM DK Shivakumar tells ASHA workers
stories.deck: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar addressed ASHA workers during their ongoing protest for a salary increase. He expressed the government's commitment to meet their demands while avoiding any formal written guarantees. The CM highlighted the need for trust in verbal commitments and criticized the interference of political leaders. He emphasized that the government has made progress on four of…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU/MYSURU: After making three appeals in a week, Karnataka chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 assured ASHA workers, whose day-and-night agitation for a monthly honorarium of Rs 15,000 entered its 10th day on Thursday, that govt will fulfil all their demands but ruled out making any written assurances.
On the sidelines of a Constitution Day event at Vidhana Soudha, the CM said, “Do not threaten the govt. ASHA workers should first set aside their pride. Others are using them for their own politics and they will not help them. There are serious issues involved. The workers are not alone.”
Requesting “our mothers” to end the protest, the CM targeted 
BJP
 leaders for backing the strike and questioned their silence on the role of the Centre.
“I can’t give a written assurance to the protesting workers. This is not a contract. Why is no one asking the Centre for a written reply? Isn’t the Centre also responsible for meeting these demands? If there is no trust in the words of the chief minister, I can do nothing. Even the govt has its limits,” he said.
The Congress govt, the CM said, has delivered on its promises and would continue to find solutions to workers’ problems. 
Govt has already made four of the five guarantee schemes available for ASHA workers, he said, reaffirming that govt is sympathetic to workers.
Shivakumar said no govt can be blackmailed, while buying time to discuss the issue during the Belagavi legislature session. The ASHA workers’ demand for revised honorarium is not wrong. Govt had increased it once and would hike it again, he added.
The CM said workers from 17 departments have made similar pay-hike demands.
On health minister UT Khader’s reported statement that work would continue without ASHA workers, Shivakumar said there was no truth to that. “We need everyone. The minister’s statement has been misinterpreted,” he added.

stories.headline: SIR: In Karnataka’s electoral rolls, thousands of parents are younger than their children
stories.deck: More than 17,000 entries in the final SIR rolls show parents listed as younger than or the same age as their children, while thousands of others have an age gap of less than 15 years — discrepancies the SIR was intended to identify and correct
stories.bodyText:
A 70-year-old man is listed as the “son of a 59-year-old” in Karnataka’s final electoral rolls. In other instance, a 40-year-old man is listed as the father of another 40-year-old man, with both registered at the same address.
Both are among entries in the final electoral rolls where a parent is either younger than or the same age as their child or has an age gap of “less than 15 years” with the child. The Hindu found more than 17,000 such entries in its analysis.
Krishnoji, a resident of the BBMP South district, is listed as 59, while his son, Gowtham, is 70. Both are listed at the same house number in Polling Station 180 of Govindarajanagar Assembly constituency. In Bidar’s Aurad Assembly constituency, Mallapa and his son, Ramesh, are both listed as 40. They are registered at the same house and in the same polling station.
The analysis of the final electoral rolls — published on the Chief Electoral Officer’s Karnataka website — found that these discrepancies are spread across the State, with the highest numbers in Raichur, Kalaburagi, and Yadgir. Raichur has 1,960 such entries, while Kalaburagi has more than 1,700.
A district-wise break=up further shows that in at least 2,200 entries across Karnataka, the father is listed as “one to five years younger” than the child. In Kalaburagi, for instance, Baramanna is listed as 45, while his son, Gundappa, is 50. Both are listed at the same address in the Jewargi Assembly constituency.
In thousands of other cases, the age gap between the parent and the child is less than 15. The Hindu found that in at least 5,100 entries, the gap was between six and 10 years, and in another 3,000, it was between one and five years. For example, Hucchappa, an elector in Ballari, is listed as 76, while his son, Eranna, is 69. Both are listed at the same address in the Kampli Assembly constituency.
Logical discrepancy
It is important to note that an “age gap of less than 15 years between a parent and progeny” was one of the nine logical discrepancies identified during the SIR in Karnataka. More than 43 lakh people across the State were served notices over the nine categories of logical discrepancies and asked to attend hearings to establish the correctness of their details.
Officials had previously said that an “age gap of less than 15 years between a parent and progeny” was considered implausible and could point to errors in dates of birth in documents such as Aadhaar. The criterion was included to identify and correct such errors during the SIR. People flagged for this discrepancy, besides others, were asked to appear for hearings and justify the details. However, analysis of the final rolls shows that thousands of entries with such age gaps continue to figure in the final rolls.
The Hindu mailed a few sample cases to the CEO’s office, which said it would verify them.

stories.headline: Four-member gang targeting cab, bike taxi drivers arrested in Bengaluru
stories.deck: Gang allegedly committed over 30 robberies in three months to fund drug purchases; police trace 11 cases
stories.bodyText:
The Whitefield police have busted an extortion racket and arrested four men who allegedly targeted cab and bike taxi drivers at night, assaulted them, and extorted money. The gang is suspected of having committed over two dozen such robberies in the past three months to fund their drug addiction and other vices.
The accused have been identified as Manoj, Preetham Prakash, Syed Shafi, and Akhilesh, residents of Gandhipura and Vijayanagar in Whitefield.
The arrests followed a complaint by Mohammed Nisar, a bike rider, who was allegedly intercepted and assaulted by the accused on an isolated stretch near Nallurhalli Metro station. The accused, who arrived in a car, allegedly assaulted him and forced him to transfer money online from his mobile phone before fleeing.
Following the complaint, a team of Whitefield police, led by DCP Haribabu, launched an operation to track down the gang.
The police traced the rental aggregator through which the accused had hired the car and followed the vehicle for around 2 km to 3 km. As the accused allegedly drove at high speed to evade the police, the investigators sought the rental company’s assistance in remotely switching off the car’s engine.
When the vehicle came to a halt, the accused stepped out to check the engine. Police personnel surrounded the car and arrested three of them on the spot. The fourth accused, who initially managed to escape, was arrested later.
The probe revealed that all four accused were drug users and allegedly committed the robberies to raise money to buy narcotics. The money extorted from drivers was reportedly transferred directly to the bank account of a suspected drug peddler.
Manoj, the prime accused, allegedly planned the robberies and identified potential targets. Preetham Prakash, a BCom graduate, was his associate, while Syed Shafi worked as a cab driver and Akhilesh was employed as a tattoo artist.
The gang initially used an autorickshaw to commit the robberies but later switched to a rented car to target drivers.
During interrogation, the accused allegedly confessed to committing around 30 robberies in three months. The police have so far traced and linked the gang to 11 incidents.
Investigators are also identifying other victims, as several drivers who lost relatively small amounts of money had not approached the police to file complaints.

briefs.headline: Karnataka govt steps up food testing as Bengaluru’s eateries multiply
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Karnataka
 has sharply intensified food testing and enforcement in the past two years, with the state analysing nearly 1.2 lakh samples between 2022-23 and Oct 30, 2026, amid growing concerns over quality and hygiene in Bengaluru’s rapidly expanding food and hospitality sector.
Of the nearly 1.2 lakh samples tested during the period, 1,769 failed the prescribed standards. The findings led to proceedings before adjudicating authorities and courts, with some cases still pending.
Food safety department data shows that testing increased significantly from 2024-25. The number of samples analysed rose from 6,851 in 2022-23 and 9,172 in 2023-24 to 45,696 in 2024-25 — a nearly five-fold jump from the previous year. Testing stood at 39,762 in 2025-26. The decline in testing was mainly due to a fall in surveillance sampling as the department focused on enforcement. In the current financial year, 18,105 samples had been tested as of Oct 30.
Food safety came into sharper focus following the efforts of food safety and drug administration commissioner Srinivas K and health minister UT Khader. The move assumes greater significance in Bengaluru, where lakhs of restaurants, food outlets and streetside establishments cater to a large and constantly expanding population.
Srinivas, while speaking to 
TOI
 on the sidelines of the National Conference on Food Safety and Drug Regulation here Thursday, said inspections and testing had been intensified from 2024-25 using the available infrastructure and manpower.
“From 2024-25, we rigorously increased inspections and testing with the available infrastructure and staff. Testing is a continuous process and the numbers keep getting added as the year progresses. Enforcement sampling, which involves first-time testing, has also increased from 2024-25. This financial year, we still have a good 4-5 months left, and both enforcement and testing numbers will increase,” he said.
Of the 1,769 samples that failed the prescribed tests during the period, 1,197 cases were registered before the assistant drugs controller, while 572 were filed before judicial magistrate first class (JMFC) courts.
Officials said the cases included samples that resulted in suspension, notices or penalties. However, some violations were minor and resulted only in notices being issued to the establishments concerned.
Penalties collected through enforcement proceedings have also risen steadily. The department collected Rs 14.6 lakh in 2022-23, Rs 59 lakh in 2024-25, and Rs 65.2 lakh in 2025-26. As much as Rs 45.4 lakh was collected in 2026-27 as on Oct 30.
Food sector expands rapidly, active licences rise to 4.2L
The number of food businesses operating under the state’s licensing and registration framework has risen 53% in four years, reflecting the rapid expansion of the state’s food sector and efforts to bring more establishments under the food-safety net.
Active food licences and registrations increased from 2.7 lakh in 2022-23 to 4.2 lakh in 2026-27. The growth has been steady each year, rising to 3 lakh in 2023-24 and 3.4 lakh in 2024-25 before exceeding the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India’s (
FSSAI
) target of 3.5 lakh in 2025-26. Karnataka recorded 3.7 lakh active licences and registrations that year, reaching 105% of the target. The figure climbed further to 4,21,560 in 2026-27, taking the state to 120% of the FSSAI target. Karnataka now has over 71,000 active licences and registrations above the prescribed target.
The rise points to the growing number of restaurants, eateries, street-food establishments, and other food businesses across the state, particularly in Bengaluru, where the food and hospitality sector has expanded rapidly. Department officials attributed the increase to sustained efforts to bring more food businesses into the formal food-safety framework through licensing and registration. The move is also aimed at ensuring that a larger share of food establishments is covered by inspections, testing and enforcement.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru dental students allege private colleges charge Rs 15,000–38,000 for mandatory internships, then pay low stipends
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Dental students from several private colleges have alleged that their institutions are charging between Rs 15,000 and Rs 38,000 for mandatory internships while paying them only nominal stipends.
A one-year internship is mandatory after the BDS (Bachelor of Dental Surgery) final examination, and students are to be paid stipends during the period. Students alleged that colleges were charging all interns irrespective of their admission quota. “This varies from Rs 15,000 to Rs 38,000. In return, the students are paid Rs 1,000-Rs 2,000 as stipends. How is this even justifiable? The colleges charge all students, irrespective of the quota they have taken admission in. This is fleecing students,” said a student.
Another student said a college had demanded Rs 15,000 in advance while paying a stipend of Rs 1,250.
A student from another institution alleged that the college was collecting Rs 36,000 and paying Rs 3,000 monthly as a stipend. The college issued receipts in case of inspections, he said.
Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences (RGUHS) said it has not received any formal complaint. 
“The university will not tolerate colleges taking any money from students outside what is lawfully permitted,” vice-chancellor Bhagavan BC said. “We have, time and again, issued circulars to colleges to ensure that internships are held properly for all courses. Students have to be paid stipends properly. They need to be given facilities they deserve like duty room, clean bathroom, well-lit corridors. Their duty hours should not exceed 8-12 hours at a stretch. Despite these circulars, if we find colleges to be flouting norms, we will initiate action against them.”
There are 39 dental colleges with an annual intake of around 2,700 seats. With BDS back in demand, in the past two years, all the seats have been picked up by students. The fees for dental programmes range from Rs 49,350 in govt colleges to Rs 8 lakh for management seats in private colleges.

briefs.headline: Dirty backlog: Half of Bengaluru’s sewage still untreated, but 45 treatment plants in the pipeline
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Nearly half the sewage the city generates daily is not treated properly, and the full fix is about three years away, according to Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB).
The city produces about 2,580 million litres per day (MLD) of sewage, but BWSSB’s 34 sewage treatment plants (STPs) can treat only 1,348.5 MLD. That leaves 1,231.5 MLD left entirely or inadequately treated.
As per the water authority, 45 new STPs with a combined capacity of 1,163 MLD will be added in phases between Dec 2026 and Sept 2029. Only 117 MLD of this is due by the end of this year, while the largest addition — 335 MLD from four plants — comes at the very end of the schedule.
A senior official said: “Bengaluru’s growth has outpaced its water and sewage infrastructure, and we’re working on both fronts at once. Today, the city’s demand is met only because borewells supply about 800 MLD of water alongside the Cauvery; that balance will not hold as population rises. That’s why we’re adding Cauvery Stage VI, expanding reuse of treated wastewater, promoting rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge, and cutting distribution losses.
”
When asked about quality assessment, the board said an independent end-to-end audit of water quality standards was under way, while the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) was separately assessing the quality framework to validate the findings.
“An independent audit of treated water quality is under way, alongside an IISc assessment, because capacity alone isn’t enough. Our real-time dashboard already tracks compliance with KSPCB (pollution control board) norms. A master plan up to 2046 will guide investment in the newly added areas,” the official added.
BWSSB said it is expanding its sewage treatment infrastructure in the long run through multiple funding sources, including the 
World Bank
 (nine STPs, Rs 1,000 crore), Urban Challenge Fund (nine STPs, Rs 1,350 crore), and JICA (14 STPs, Rs 968 crore). The board said these projects would help bridge the gap between sewage generation and treatment and prevent pollution of waterbodies.
DEMAND & SUPPLY (2026)
* Water demand: 2,650 MLD
* Supply: 2,720 MLD
* Surplus: 70 MLD
Where water comes from
* Cauvery: 1,920 MLD
* Borewells: ~800 MLD
* Without borewells, city would face deficit of ~730 MLD
WHAT’S REQUIRED (As per BWSSB)
* Bengaluru Metropolitan Region faces a 3,600-MLD water deficit
* 4,000-4,500 MLD of supply and savings possible by 2037
* Rs 25,500-crore investment needed
1. Bulk water
* Cauvery Stage VI: 500 MLD (₹7,000-crore investment)
* Yettinahole: 50 MLD (counted within the ₹7,000 crore)
* Network optimisation: 50-100 MLD (₹300 crore)
* 550 MLD of extra supply planned to serve peri-urban towns
2. Treated water reuse
* Industries and institutions: 900-1,100 MLD (₹1,200 crore)
* Agriculture: 800-900 MLD (₹1,500 crore)
* 2,000 MLD of new tertiary treatment capacity
* 150km purple network linking STPs to hubs
* 40+ storage tanks and a canal network
3. Agricultural water optimisation
* Saves 300-400 MLD (₹2,500 crore)
* Drip and micro-irrigation in command areas
* Shift to less water-intensive crops
4. Groundwater recharge
* Adds 1,100-1,200 MLD of water (₹5,000 crore)
* Lake rejuvenation and aquifer recharge
* Recharge wells and stormwater harvesting
5. Non-revenue water reduction
* Saves 300-400 MLD (₹5,000 crore)
* District Metered Area-based metering and leak detection
* Pressure management and pipeline replacement

briefs.headline: AITUC National Conference in Bengaluru concludes with calls to defend Constitution, implement scientific minimum wages
briefs.deck: Recognising the rapid expansion of gig and platform employment, the Conference also resolved to intensify efforts to organise, unionise and unite platform-based gig workers
briefs.bodyText:
The 43rd National Conference of the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC), which concluded on Thursday in Bengaluru, strongly condemned the four Labour Codes and demanded scientific minimum wages for all workers.
Arguing that the Labour Codes weaken collective bargaining, trade union rights, statutory safeguards and the right to strike, while facilitating corporate exploitation, the trade union leadership expressed serious concern over ‘growing contractorisation, outsourcing, fragmentation of the workforce, and the denial of permanent employment’.
“These practices deliberately divide workers, weaken collective strength and undermine trade union organisation,” they said.
Scientific minimum wages needed
A major demand made during the conference was scientific minimum wages for all workers based on the 15th Indian Labour Conference recommendations, Dr. Aykroyd’s nutritional requirements and Supreme Court guidelines.
The union leaders pointed out that it reaffirmed universal social security for all working people, particularly those in the unorganised sector, as a guaranteed right and not an act of charity.
Unionisation of gig workers
Recognising the rapid expansion of gig and platform employment, the conference also resolved to intensify efforts to organise, unionise and unite platform-based gig workers as an integral part of the working class.
At its session held in the city in 1983, the AITUC made a call to ‘organise the unorganised‘ making it an organisational priority. Recalling this, the conference called for a renewed nationwide campaign to organise gig and platform workers.
New leadership
The conference unanimously elected a General Council of 364 members and a Working Committee of 91 members. K. Subbarayan, MP, was unanimously elected president, and Amarjeet Kaur was re-elected as general secretary.
Forty-seven resolutions covering national, sectoral, and international issues concerning the working class were adopted during the conference. Sixty-eight delegates participated in the commission deliberations.
The conference’s political report examined the deepening crisis of ‘global capitalism, imperialist aggression, militarisation and wars, including the continuing assault on Palestine and the Russia-Ukraine war’, and called for strengthening international solidarity against ‘imperialism, militarism and the growing influence of extreme right-wing and authoritarian forces’.
The leadership condemned the Indian government’s pro-corporate economic policies, which, they argued, concentrate wealth with a few, undermine the public sector and intensify exploitation of workers. They also asserted that communal polarisation and neoliberal economic policies are two inseparable instruments of the same offensive.
Concluding on Constitution Day, the conference underlined that defending the constitutional values of equality, liberty and fraternity is inseparable from the struggle for workers’ rights and a society free from exploitation.

briefs.headline: Black Kite rescued near Bannerghatta in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Avian and Reptile Rehabilitation Centre (ARCC) has rescued a Black Kite that had been hanging from a high-tension power line near Bannerghatta.
ARCC said that the bird had been hanging from a high-tension power line at a height of over 90 feet since November 23.
It said the bird was trapped on a 400kV line, making the rescue particularly challenging. The rescue operation began around 5.30 a.m. on Thursday.
“We then started working with Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation (KPTCL) to find a way to rescue the bird safely. Initially, we were told that the power supply could only be switched off at night. The line supplies electricity to nearly ten areas of Bengaluru, making a daytime shutdown difficult to arrange,” ARCC said.
As a video of the bird was already going viral on Instagram, ARCC said they were worried that members of the public might attempt to rescue it themselves.
“Apart from the risk to the bird, anyone attempting to reach a live high-tension line could face a potentially fatal electric shock. We wanted to find a way to intervene before someone put their own life at risk,” it added.
KPTCL arranged a specialised insulated aerial work platform, imported from Brazil, which could reach the bird without interrupting the power supply.
“After hours of coordination and preparation, the Black Kite was successfully rescued at 1 p.m. from the high-tension line, without disrupting electricity supply to the areas served by it.
It was a challenging operation that brought together members of the general public, rescue organisations, the Forest Department and the KPTCL department to find a solution where a conventional rescue was not possible,” ARCC said.
The rescued bird has suffered injuries and is at present undergoing treatment.

briefs.headline: Only 30% wear helmets, 24% exceed speed limits: Study highlights road safety risks in Karnataka
briefs.deck: According to the report, helmet use in Bengaluru region, between 2022 and 2026, has declined from 88% to 56%.
briefs.bodyText:
Highlighting the high road safety risks in Karnataka, a recent study has found that only around 15% of motorcyclists in the State wear helmets correctly, while overall helmet usage stands at just 30%.
The study, titled Status Summary Report 2026: Karnataka State, India, also reveals how road safety violations are much higher in the rest of the State compared to the Bengaluru region.
Speeding State
The baseline study, conducted between December 2025 and June 2026, analysed more than one million road users and vehicle observations across 48 observation sites for three risk factors, including speed, helmet use, and seat-belt and child restraint use. Johns Hopkins International Injury Research Unit (JH-IIRU) provided technical support along with NIMHANS for the study, under the Bloomberg Philanthropies Initiative for Global Road Safety.
According to the study, 24% of observed vehicles exceeded the posted speed limit. Speeding was higher in the rest of Karnataka (25%) than in the Bengaluru Metropolitan Region (18%), and higher on weekends (26%) than weekdays (21%).
Around 4% of drivers used a handheld phone while driving. Speeding was most commonly spotted among sedans, SUVs, light vehicles and pickup/light trucks.
Helmet and seat belt use
According to the report , helmet use in Bengaluru region, between 2022 and 2026, has declined from 88% to 56%, while correct helmet use has fallen from 34% to 25%. (Correct use refers to wearing a standardised full-face or half-face helmet securely fastened.)
The study also found that helmet use was much lower in the rest of the State (22%) compared to that in Bengaluru Metropolitan Region (56%). Correct helmet use was found to be substantially lower among pillion rides (5%) than drivers (19%).
While around 22% adults used seatbelts, the use was higher among drivers (30%) than other occupants (22%). Significant geographical disparities were observed between Bengaluru and the rest of the State in terms of seat belt use too. While 40% in Bengaluru Metropolitan Region used seat belts, the percentage was found to be just 15% in the rest of Karnataka.
Child restraint use was observed as consistently less than 1%, exposing young children travelling in vehicles to serious risks.
‘Department will encourage behavioural surveillance’
The report was launched at NIMHANS, in the presence of Y.C. Janardhana Reddy, Director,- NIMHANS; Ramendra Pratap Shukla, Director, Road Safety at the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways; K. Parashurama, Commissioner for Traffic and Road Safety, Karnataka State Police, and Gopal M. Byakod, DCP Traffic, Bengaluru Traffic Police.
“The police department will encourage and support the need to make behavioural surveillance a routine in road safety action plans, making enforcement smarter and targeted to address the key risk factors like speed and helmet use. The system also needs to make helmets affordable to every rider. State and district action plans must target higher compliance and reduction in the number of crashes and injuries each year,” said Mr. Parashuram.
Mr. Shukla noted that the Karnataka government must be applauded for a marginal reduction in the overall number of crashes, adding that nationally, however, deaths due to incorrect helmet use have increased marginally.

briefs.headline: Karnataka seeks national portal to track substandard drugs
briefs.bodyText:
Karnataka’s Food Safety and Drugs Controller Srinivas K. called for a national portal to track Not of Standard Quality (NSQ) medicines by integrating test results from government and private drug-testing laboratories across the country.
Speaking at a national conference on Food Safety and Drug Administration attended by Central and State regulators, he said Karnataka had around 53 private drug-testing laboratories besides government facilities. However, results from private laboratories were not adequately integrated into the regulatory information network.
He proposed a common platform that would enable private laboratories to upload test results and regulators across States to access the data. This would help identify substandard medicines early, facilitate coordinated recalls, and prevent NSQ drugs from re-entering the market through other distribution channels.
Faster action against NSQ medicines
Mr. Srinivas said the State had introduced an e-sign-based system to speed up the transmission of laboratory reports and regulatory action. Earlier, generating Form 13 after a drug was declared NSQ and forwarding the report through the regulatory hierarchy could take around 10 days. The digital system had substantially reduced the delay.
The State had also introduced a mechanism to block the distribution chain of identified NSQ medicines up to the distributor level. It had undertaken a pilot quality assessment of medical facilities in Chikkaballapur district to identify deficiencies and recommend corrective measures.
He also sought dedicated testing facilities for medical devices and injectable products.
Stronger inter-State coordination
Health Minister U.T. Khader, who inaugurated the conference, said medicines and food products crossed State borders, making stronger inter-State coordination, real-time information sharing, and uniform national standards essential.
He cited the ongoing SIT investigation into a counterfeit medicine network involving approximately ₹5 crore, with financial trails exceeding ₹18 crore, as an example of the need for stringent enforcement.

stories.headline: Gold price crash puts pledged jewellery at risk as lenders issue auction notices
stories.deck: Nearly 40% of the gold-loan portfolios of these lenders have reportedly breached the thresholds, with the ratio exceeding 95% in some cases. The notices ask borrowers to either repay a portion of their outstanding dues or furnish additional collateral to bring their LTV ratios back within the prescribed limits. Failure to do so could result in the pledged gold jewellery being auctioned
stories.bodyText:
With 
gold prices
 crashing, gold-loan companies have begun sending legal auction notices to borrowers. The sharp decline in gold prices over the past two weeks has pushed loan-to-value (LTV) ratios beyond permissible limits.
Gold prices have dropped 35% from their January peak and 11% so far in November, as markets factor in the possibility of higher US policy rates. The prospect of rising rates has reduced the appeal of gold, which does not generate any yield. According to lenders, the steep correction has triggered margin calls for a substantial number of customers for the first time in around four years.
Gold loan notices
Nearly 40% of the gold-loan portfolios of these lenders have reportedly breached the thresholds, with the ratio exceeding 95% in some cases.
The notices ask borrowers to either repay a portion of their outstanding dues or furnish additional collateral to bring their LTV ratios back within the prescribed limits. Failure to do so could result in the pledged gold jewellery being auctioned, according to an ET report.
Banks and gold-loan financiers, including Muthoot and Manappuram, have told the 
Reserve Bank of India
 (RBI) that they have lowered the LTV ratio for new loans as a precautionary measure.
The average has been reduced to 60%-65% from around 75%, providing lenders with a greater buffer against any further decline in gold prices, the people cited above said.
In gold lending, a breach of the LTV limit is treated as a borrower default, even when the borrower has not missed a scheduled repayment.
Executives at lending companies, who requested anonymity, said they are contacting affected borrowers and giving them the option of pledging additional gold or making an upfront payment to cover the margin shortfall before proceeding with an auction. Gold auctions are conducted 30 days after a legal notice has been served.
Gold loans are generally short-term facilities, with borrowers often repaying the principal in a lump sum at the end of the tenure. Given this repayment structure, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has instructed lenders to ensure that the value of pledged gold remains adequate to cover the outstanding principal, accumulated interest and auction-related expenses throughout the loan period.
Senior executives at major gold-loan companies said they are keeping a close watch on their portfolios, moderating fresh disbursements and stepping up collection efforts. They also warned that auctions could increase if borrowers fail to meet margin calls.
Lenders generally maintain an effective loan-to-value (LTV) ratio of around 85% when customers pay interest every month. Where interest is settled at the end of the loan tenure, the ratio is typically kept lower, at 70%-72%.
Additional collateral
The fall in gold prices has pushed up LTV ratios as the value of the pledged jewellery has declined. Consider a lender that provides a loan of Rs 75,000 against gold worth Rs 1 lakh. The initial LTV in this case would be 75%. If the collateral loses 15% of its value, the ratio would rise to approximately 88%. A 25% fall would push it to 100%, even if the borrower’s outstanding loan amount remained unchanged.
Data from credit information company CRIF show that the gold-loan portfolio had grown to around Rs 23 lakh crore as of September 30, representing approximately 12% of the country's Rs 185 lakh crore retail-loan market.
The RBI's concern stems from the fact that a significant part of this expansion has been driven by existing customers borrowing larger amounts, renewing their loans and taking additional credit through top-ups. This growth has not been matched by a comparable rise in the number of borrowers or the volume of gold pledged, according to the ET report.
Figures published by the Indian Bullion and Jewellers’ Association (IBJA) show that the price of 999-purity gold in India fell to Rs 1,21,038 per 10 grams on a rolling one-month basis, from the evening closing rate of Rs 1,41,710 per 10 grams on October 26.
International gold prices have also declined sharply. The metal's price in US dollars per troy ounce fell 13% over one month and more than 25% over three months to $3,481, according to the latest data from investing.com.
Meanwhile, the dollar index, which measures the US currency's strength against a basket of major global currencies, is hovering near its highest level in about two years. It traded close to 104 late Wednesday. A reading above 100 indicates relative strength in the dollar, which can reduce the attractiveness of assets denominated in other currencies.

briefs.headline: Rupee in undervalued territory in October despite modest gains
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: The rupee’s inflation-adjusted trade-determined value (the real effective exchange rate or REER) recovered marginally in Oct, with the index rising to 93.14 from 92.14 a month earlier. The currency remained undervalued against its 40 trading partners, but the modest rebound suggests that some of the ground lost in recent months was being recovered.
The undervaluation appears to explain 
RBI
’s comfort with the sharp strengthening of the rupee in Nov despite the backdrop of rising imports and a widening trade deficit.
The month-on-month recovery followed RBI’s Oct 7 repo rate hike of 25 basis points to 5.5% and tighter currency derivatives rules introduced on Oct 10, which eased immediate pressure on the rupee. Over the 12 months to Oct 2026, the 40-currency REER fell from 97.14 to 93.14.
The decline was also evident in the narrower six-currency basket, based on the revised 2022-23 base year, where the index dropped from 93.97 in Oct 2025 to 89.99 in Oct 2026. This points to a sustained weakening in the rupee’s inflation-adjusted value against its trading partners.
RBI calculates the nominal effective exchange rate (NEER) using two trade-weighted baskets of foreign currencies, comprising 40 currencies and a narrower basket of six. The weights reflect India’s trade with each partner. A fall in the rupee against major trading currencies such as the dollar and euro pulls down the NEER.
The REER adjusts the NEER for differences in inflation between India and its trading partners, using consumer price index data.

At the same time, gross FDI into the country fell 18% to $5.9 billion during Sept.
The net FDI numbers are the worst in several months, while the gross inflow numbers are the lowest since January, according to data released by RBI. September 2025 also saw net FDI outflows of around $3 billion.
During the first half of the year, however, net FDI was 20% at $8.8 billion as gross inflows rose 14% to $60.1 billion. Outward FDI was up 18.2% to $22 billion during this period, while repatriation went up 12% to almost $30 billion. Officials said that some of the outflow is on account of overseas investors cashing out in some of the IPOs, while in a few cases Indian companies have bought a part of the equity held by their overseas partners. Govt is, however, confident of achieving the gross FDI target of $100 billion during the current fiscal.

briefs.headline: Know IBEF? Entity accused of creating excess capacity
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: “IBEF (India Brand Equity Foundation) is the major implementing vehicle for investment and export promotion of govt of India,” said USTR’s section 301 report, which proposed 25% additional tariffs on India, while identifying the agency as a key pillar in India’s push for creating "structural excess capacity" and putting on a par with the Rs 2 lakh crore production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme.
USTR, which has extensively quoted govt-run IBEF, has catapulted it from a corner of Barakhamba Road to the prominence that is usually reserved for giant export promotion vehicles, such as Japan External Trade Organisation (JETRO) or Austrade.
Quite rich and lavish for an initiative whose Rs 260 crore corpus is spartan even by India’s standards. Details notwithstanding, it points to an effort to hammer out an indictment and then frame an argument around it.
While most are aware of PLI -- a key govt initiative to boost manufacturing in sectors such as electronics, pharma and processed food -- majority are unlikely to have heard of IBEF, an entity set up in 1996 for promoting Brand India. It has survived UPA and NDA regimes, albeit with periodic makeovers.
IBEF describes itself as “a knowledge centre for global investors, international policy-makers and world media seeking updated, accurate and comprehensive information on the Indian economy, states and sectors”. 
It’s last uploaded annual report for 2024-25 lists out several promotion initiatives such as those related to basmati rice, millets, geographical indications. Besides, it highlights its digital media initiatives -- including setting up the commerce department’s social media cell.
 The agency is run by a govt-controlled board, which has secretaries from commerce and DPIIT as directors.
While accusing India of undertaking policies and practices to create “structural excess capacity”, the USTR report said: “Implementing industrial plans to maintain and expand Indian manufacturing, setting overall targets for manufacturing and exports, such as 
Make in India
, Production Linked Incentives, Atmanirbhar Bharat (self-reliant India), and IBEF, including by offering financial incentives to eligible companies based on their incremental sales.”
It also alleged that India is tolerating inadequate labour protections, maintaining market barriers and imposing financial repression policies that have the effect of suppressing interest rates or of directing the allocation of equity and debt in a manner that results in outcomes different from those that would reflect market-oriented conditions.
